Sure, here's a recipe for rigatoni with hearty sausage ragu:

Ingredients:

* 1 pound rigatoni pasta
* 2 tablespoons olive oil
* 1 onion, finely chopped
* 3 garlic cloves, minced
* 1 pound sweet Italian sausage, casings removed
* 1 can (28 oz) crushed tomatoes
* 1 cup beef broth
* 1 teaspoon dried basil
* Salt and freshly ground black pepper
* Grated Parmesan cheese, for serving
* Fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish

Instructions:

1. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook the rigatoni according to package instructions until al dente. Reserve 1 cup of pasta cooking water before draining.
2. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute.
3. Add the sweet Italian sausage to the skillet, breaking it up with a spoon as it cooks, until browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes.
4. Add the crushed tomatoes, beef broth, dried basil, salt, and black pepper to the skillet. Stir to combine and bring the sauce to a simmer. Reduce the heat to low and let it cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, allowing the flavors to meld together and the sauce to thicken slightly.
5. When the rigatoni is done cooking, add it to the skillet with the sauce, tossing everything together to ensure the pasta is well coated. If the sauce seems too thick, you can add some of the reserved pasta cooking water to thin it out.
6. Serve the rigatoni hot, topped with grated Parmigiano Reggiano cheese and garnished with chopped fresh pars

> Lorenzo Sumulong Tañada (June 10, 1908 – August 23, 1980) was a Filipino lawyer and politician who served as Senator for the Liberal Party in the Philippines from 1947 to 1965 and again from 1967 until his death in 1980. He also served as Speaker of the House of Representatives during the Second Republic from 1943-1944.
>
> ## Early life[edit]
>
> Born on June 10, 1908 in Manila, he was the son of Manuel L. Quezon, second President of the Commonwealth of the Philippines, and Maria Agoncillo Sumulong, daughter of Don Mariano Ponce de Leon y Sumulong, one of the richest men in the country at that time.^{[1]} His mother's family were descendants of Spanish conquistador Juan de Salcedo,^{[2]} while his father's side came from Chinese immigrants.^{[3]}
>
> In 1926, he graduated with honors from Ateneo Municipal High School, now known as Ateneo de Manila University Senior High School. After graduating from high school, he went to study law at the University of Santo Tomas where he earned his Bachelor of Laws degree in 1931. While studying there, he became president of the university's student council.
>
> On July 1, 1931, he married Carmen Guerrero Nakpil, daughter of Marcelo H. del Pilar, one of the leaders of the Philippine Revolution against Spain. They had three children: Lorenzo III, Jose Conrado, and Cristina.

"The club is delighted to confirm that Michael O'Leary has agreed to a new contract", a club statement released today read. "His leadership, experience and stability have been key factors in our improving performances on the pitch. We look forward to continuing this progress under his management".

Details of the new contract, including its length, haven't been disclosed yet, but it's expected to keep O'Leary at the Villa Park for the foreseeable future.

Under O'Leary's management, Villa has developed a strong squad and adopted a bolder and more exciting playing style, which has proven popular among the fans. He has also demonstrated an eye for talent, overseeing the development of several young players who have established themselves in the first team.

Club captain Jack Grealish shared his excitement over the news, tweeting, "Can't wait for what's to come under the gaffer's lead. Let's go, Villa!"

In the wake of the announcement, many pundits have praised Villa's decision to secure O'Leary's services moving forward, citing the need for managerial stability in football, which can often see a high turnover of coaches.

Although Villa fans will be relieved to see the issue of O'Leary's future put to rest, they'll be hoping that this is just the first of many positive off-pitch developments this summer as the club looks to further secure their Premier League status and perhaps eye a push for European football.

Talks have been ongoing about potential new signings to build on last season's performances, but the players, management and fans alike can now turn their full attention to preparations for the upcoming campaign, safe in the knowledge that their man in charge is going nowhere.

Azaleas unfold blushing gowns, beneath the pecan trees,
The magnolias blossom, carried on the soft, warm breeze
Rivers carry golden pollen, the essence of the pines,
Sweet aroma fills the air from confederate jasmine vines.

Redbud trees in bloom against a clear Carolina blue,
Spanish moss gently hangs, creating an ethereal view.
Cardinals flutter, gifting spots of fiery, passionate red,
Tender footsteps of a deer, where the camellia petals spread.

Wisteria weaves a blanket, lilac clusters hanging fair,
In the field of buttercups, sunlight creates an amber glare.
Mockingbirds reciting songs, in the southern live oak’s shade,
A quartet of melody and colour, a symphony, nature-made.

The song of the cicadas echoes, as day gives into evening's hush,
Fireflies begin their dance, in the mellow dusk-light rush.
The promise of humid nights, under a moon laced with silver touch,
Such is the bewitching charm, of a southern springtime’s clutch. 

Its warmth seeps into your bones, like sweet tea on a sultry day,
Whispers of a bygone era, where hoop skirts used to sway.
Beneath the lazy sun, the south unfurls her elegant spring,
A silent invitation to partake in the enchantment she will bring.

The mystery deepens in the softness of its southern glow,
Painting magic on the landscape, a spectacle for those below.
Shimmering with life, all cloaked in a languid, honeyed hue,
Spring in the South is a poem, eternally whispering and forever new.
